verdict.rationale: Claude Code documents its own sandboxed Bash tool, which enforces OS-level filesystem and network isolation for every command and its child processes. That lets users bound what agent-run tests can touch, so production files and hosts can be kept out of reach. However, this is execution isolation, not a dedicated test or sandbox environment with separate non-production data, and nothing corroborates it independently. missing for 10: a documented test/staging environment or mock-data separation from production, explicit guidance on keeping production data untouched during testing, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the sandbox.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Claude Code's sandboxed Bash tool provides filesystem and network isolation for safer, more autonomous agent execution.
you define which files and network domains commands can touch, and the operating system enforces that boundary for every Bash command and its child processes.
